title: Female borrowers who write longer pitches may fund faster, contradicting general verbosity trends.
Female borrowers who specify the purchase of hardware like smartphones may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the loan amount in local currency may fund more slowly.
Detailed narratives regarding fleeing political instability may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Male borrowers who include personal details about family size and housing may fund faster.
Male borrowers who include the specific ages of their children may fund faster.
While referencing successful previous loan cycles accelerates funding for women, it is associated with slower funding for men.
Female borrowers who mention children and spouse may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the broader impact of the loan on family or community well-being may fund faster.
Female borrowers who include specific details about their children's ages or school status may fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of successful loans from NWTF fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Pitches that include specific geographic or biographical details predict slower funding regardless of gender.
